Work ONLY inside /opt/nxeon-wt-leadgen3 (a pre-created git worktree, branch `feature/coldemail-leadgen3`, off the Nxeon hosting platform's main repo). Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon or any other /opt/nxeon-wt-* directory — two other agents are doing similar lead-research work in parallel right now on DIFFERENT niches (one is sweeping chamber-of-commerce directories nationwide for web/marketing agencies, one is doing a different angle — see "Stay in your lane" below). `node_modules` and `.env` are symlinks to the main repo — NEVER `git add -A` (known hazard, can corrupt the main repo's real `node_modules`). Only `git add` exact file paths you changed.

## Context: a previous, smaller version of this exact task already ran successfully

A prior agent researched 3 niches and delivered 29 well-sourced B2B contacts, including 9 gaming cafes/esports centers from a single directory (findgamingcafes.com). The owner's reaction: **"29 leads is not very good, we need hundreds, if not thousands."** Your job is to scale up specifically the gaming/hosting-adjacent niche — Nxeon sells VPS hosting, dedicated servers, and GAME SERVER hosting (Minecraft, CS2, Rust, ARK, etc. — check `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` or the game-server marketing pages under `app/(marketing)/` for the exact roster of games Nxeon hosts if you want the full picture) — so the target customer profile is small businesses/organizations that would plausibly need to rent a VPS, dedicated server, or game server: gaming cafes/LAN centers, esports orgs/teams (org-level contact, not individual players), Discord community server owners who run paid/branded communities with a real business presence (a public "business inquiries" contact, not a personal DM), and small independent game-server hosting resellers or Minecraft/game server network owners who might need underlying VPS capacity.

## Your lane: gaming/esports/hosting-adjacent business niches, broadened beyond the one directory already used

1. Find MORE gaming-cafe/LAN-center directories beyond findgamingcafes.com (the prior agent only used that one) — search for other open, crawlable directories or listicles of gaming cafes/LAN centers/esports venues (check robots.txt on each candidate site before using it, same as findgamingcafes.com already was).
2. Research esports organizations with a public business-contact email on their own official site (not a personal Twitter/social DM) — many esports orgs list a "business inquiries" or "partnerships" email on their own website.
3. Research established Minecraft/game-server hosting resellers or large public game-server network owners who list a real business contact (their own "Contact us" page, not a Discord invite) — these are natural VPS/dedicated-server prospects since they may need to scale their own infrastructure.
4. For EVERY contact: visit the business's/organization's OWN website and confirm the email is genuinely published there — never trust a directory listing, aggregator, or search snippet alone. Drop any candidate you can't verify this way rather than guessing.
5. Record, for every contact: business/org name, email, and the EXACT URL(s) where you found and verified it. This provenance requirement is non-negotiable — it's the entire reason this compliance review started.

## Explicitly OUT of scope — same rules as before, no exceptions

- No personal/consumer emails, no scraping individuals' social media profiles, no personal DMs or Discord handles, no targeting private individuals (including individual streamers/players — org/business-level contacts only).
- No bypassing paywalls, CAPTCHAs, login walls, or robots.txt/ToS restrictions. If a site blocks access, skip it and move to the next source.
- No purchasing or using any third-party list/data product — your own research via WebSearch/WebFetch against openly public sources only.
- Don't pad numbers with unverifiable contacts. An honest "checked N sources, verified M good contacts" is the complete answer — don't loosely-verify or invent entries to hit a round number.

## Loading the data

Use the existing importer, exactly like the prior batch: `scripts/import-leads.ts` (wraps `lib/coldemail/import.ts` + `lib/coldemail/lead-store.ts`) with `--list "<descriptive name>" --create-list --consent --note "<how this batch was sourced>"`. Read `lib/coldemail/import.ts`'s `LeadRow`/`sourceUrl` handling first (added specifically for per-contact provenance) so each contact's source URL lands in its own `ConsentRecord.note`. This is a TEST/staging data-population exercise — no actual outbound send happens as a result of your work.

## Constraints — important

- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon-wt-leadgen3` before finishing IF you touch any app code (unlikely — this is a data-population task using the existing importer).
- Commit any code changes (not the imported data, which lives in Postgres) with a clear message. Do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging, do NOT run deploy/promote scripts.
- Report back: which directories/sources you actually used (and any you had to skip, and why), the real contact count, the `EmailList` name(s) and `ImportBatch.note` content, and confirm you committed any code changes on `feature/coldemail-leadgen3`.

- **blog.ggcircuit.com** (ggCircuit's own blog — allowed by robots.txt) — its recurring "new subscriber" roundup posts and individual venue-profile posts named real LAN centers/gaming cafes with website links, which I then visited directly to find a published email: The Esports Cave (Austin, TX), H20 Esports BV/Go!GamingLab (Netherlands), The Gilded Dragon f/k/a White Dragon Games (Wilson, NC), Top Level Gaming (OH).
- Follow-up web research on specific named venues turned up: Tech Port Gaming/Boeing Center at Tech Port (San Antonio), Level Up Gaming (Tempe, AZ), Gamelot (San Antonio).

- **Minecraft/game-server hosting resellers' own contact pages** (two required decoding Cloudflare's email-obfuscation, done via `curl` + a small XOR-decode script rather than guessing): Indernos, Best Minecraft Servers, Citadel Servers, GTXGaming, SparkedHost.

**Sources checked and explicitly skipped:**
- Yelp (403 Forbidden — bot-blocked), cybercafes.com (site unreachable/dead — connection refused)
- hostingseekers.com and serchen.com (robots.txt disallows their listing/category pages, and serchen.com explicitly blocks AI crawlers)
- webhostingtalk.com (403 Forbidden)
- Many individual candidate sites were visited and dropped for lack of a verifiable email: contact-form-only sites (connectesports.com, elitegaming.gg, takersgaming.com), dead/expired/parked domains (legendgamingcenter.com, gamecave.fi, ult-esport.com, vyralteq.com — 402, contenderesports.com), and one domain that had been resold to an unrelated business (replaycafedetroit.com now redirects to an unrelated site) — caught and rejected rather than trusted.
- Valhallan/XP League franchise-locator pages were checked but publish only phone numbers, no emails, so were dropped entirely.

I ran out of WebSearch budget (200/200) partway through, which capped further discovery breadth — with more budget this niche likely has more yield, but I did not pad the count to compensate.
